'''Dennis Malik Schröder''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|r|uː|d|ər}} {{Respell|SHROO|der}};<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023–24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 3, 2025 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517083503/https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |url-status=live}}</ref> {{IPA|de|'denɪs ˈʃʁøːdɐ}}; born 15 September 1993)<ref name=timur>{{cite web|first=Timur|last=Tinç|title=Im Namen des Vaters|url=https://www.fr.de/sport/sport-mix/namen-vaters-11274268.html|website=fr.de|date=19 January 2019|access-date=22 August 2023|language=de}}</ref> is a German professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He previously played for [[SG Braunschweig]] and [[Phantoms Braunschweig]] in Germany, before joining the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for his first five seasons in the NBA. He is the sole owner of his German hometown team, [[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|Basketball Loewen Braunschweig]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]], and had been the majority shareholder of the team since 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dennis Schroder becomes sole owner of hometown club Braunschweig|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/bbl/1062140/dennis-schroder-becomes-the-sole-owner-of-hometown-club-braunschweig/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=22 May 2020|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Crain|title=OKC Thunder's Dennis Schroder Invests In His Former German Professional Team|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/nicholascrain/2020/05/21/okc-thunders-dennis-schroder-invests-in-his-former-german-professional-team/|work=Forbes|date=21 May 2020|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref>

Debuting for the [[Germany men's national basketball team|German national team]] in 2014, Schröder helped the team to its first major medal in 17 years when Germany won bronze at the [[EuroBasket 2022|2022 EuroBasket]]. In 2023, he led the national team to their first [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|World Cup]] title at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] while being named the [[FIBA World Cup MVP]]. The following year, Schröder was the flag bearer for Germany along with [[judo]]ka [[Anna-Maria Wagner]] at [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]].<ref name="Aussiedlerbote.com">{{cite web|url=https://aussiedlerbote.de/en/statement-schroder-and-wagner-carry-the-flag-in-paris/|title=Statement: Schröder and Wagner carry the flag in Paris|publisher=Aussiedlerbote.com|language=EN|date=July 23, 2024|access-date=July 23, 2024|archive-date=23 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723214104/https://aussiedlerbote.de/en/statement-schroder-and-wagner-carry-the-flag-in-paris/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He helped Germany to a fourth place finish and was named to the [[FIBA Men's Olympics All-Star Five|FIBA Olympics All-Star Five team]]. In 2025, he led Germany to the [[EuroBasket 2025]] title.

==Early life==
Schröder is the son of an ethnic German father named Axel Schröder who played basketball in Gambia before meeting Schroder's [[The Gambia|Gambian]] mother Fatou, who gave birth to eldest brother Talha and the younger daughter Farida. Schröder has two elder half-siblings from Fatou's previous marriage before relocating to Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bhaumik|first=Gayatri|title=Who is Dennis Schröder? ==Professional career==
===Phantoms Braunschweig (2010–2013)===
Schröder started playing professional basketball in 2010 for [[SG Braunschweig]], [[farm team]] of [[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|Phantoms Braunschweig]]. In his first season with SUM Baskets Braunschweig, he averaged 7.8 points, 2.1 assists and 1.6 rebounds per game in a second-tier German league. In the 2011–12 season he made a breakthrough, averaging 17.8 points and 6.7 assists over 23 regular-season games. His team went in the playoffs where he averaged 18.8 points and 5.1 assists over four games. In the same season, he also played 30 games for Phantoms Braunschweig of the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German league]], averaging 2.3 points, 0.7 assists and 0.8 rebounds in about 8 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/events/top-four/beko-bbl-top-four-2012/news/beko-bbl-top-four-2011/nyp-braunschweig.html|title=Stats 2011–12|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707003601/http://www.beko-bbl.de/events/top-four/beko-bbl-top-four-2012/news/beko-bbl-top-four-2011/nyp-braunschweig.html|archive-date=7 July 2013|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

In the 2012–13 season he played 32 games for Phantoms Braunschweig, averaging 12 points, 3.2 assists and 2.5 rebounds in 25 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/events/top-four/beko-bbl-top-four-2012/news/beko-bbl-top-four-2011/nyp-braunschweig.html|title=Stats 2012–13|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707003601/http://www.beko-bbl.de/events/top-four/beko-bbl-top-four-2012/news/beko-bbl-top-four-2011/nyp-braunschweig.html|archive-date=7 July 2013|url-status=usurped}}</ref> For the season, he was named the [[Basketball Bundesliga Most Improved Player|League's Most Improved Player]] as well as [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|Best Young German Player]].<ref name="Awards">{{cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/news/news.html/shooting-star-dennis-schroeder-ist-der-beste-deutsche-nachwuchsspieler-und-zugleich-der-most-improved-player.html|title=Shooting Star Dennis Schröder ist der "Most Improved Player" und der "Beste deutsche Nachwuchsspieler" (in German)|access-date=24 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605063311/http://www.beko-bbl.de/news/news.html/shooting-star-dennis-schroeder-ist-der-beste-deutsche-nachwuchsspieler-und-zugleich-der-most-improved-player.html|archive-date=5 June 2013|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

In 2013, Schröder was announced to play at the 2013 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] for the World Select Team. Before officially playing at the Nike Hoop Summit, Schröder decided to declare for the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{citation needed|date=April 2021}} On 20 April 2013, Schröder led his team to a 112–98 win. He finished with 18 points, 6 assists and 2 rebounds in 29 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/misc/13_hsum_box_score.pdf|title=2013 Nike Hoop Summit Boxscore|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424064318/http://www.usabasketball.com/misc/13_hsum_box_score.pdf|archive-date=24 April 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 16 September 2022, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] signed Schröder to a one-year, $2.64 million deal for his return to the team. Schröder chose the Lakers over the [[Toronto Raptors]] and [[Phoenix Suns]] citing "unfinished business" with the [[Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2022 |title=Free agent guard Dennis Schroder signs with Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/news/free-agent-guard-dennis-schroder-signs-1-year-deal-with-lakers |access-date=16 September 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 September 2022 |title=Dennis Schroeder passed on Raptors, Suns |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/dennis-schroeder-passed-on-raptors-suns/ |access-date=11 December 2022 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US |archive-date=11 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211223115/https://hoopshype.com/rumor/dennis-schroeder-passed-on-raptors-suns/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Erin |date=17 September 2022 |title=NBA Rumors: Dennis Schröder Considered Suns, Raptors Before Rejoining Lakers |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10049240-nba-rumors-dennis-schroder-considered-suns-raptors-before-rejoining-lakers |access-date=11 December 2022 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> After completing his first practice on his second stint with the team, he claimed during the media interviews that the [[Lakers]] never offered him a four-year, $84 million contract extension that he was eligible to sign during the previous free agency before the start of the [[2021–22 NBA season]].<ref name="ESPN"/>

Schröder scored 14 of his season-high 32 points in the fourth quarter to lead the Lakers to a 112–109 win over the [[Miami Heat]] during their regular season game on 4 January 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Schröder propels Lakers past Heat 112–109 without LeBron, AD|date=4 January 2023|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468729|access-date=5 January 2023}}</ref> and on 20 January 2023, he put up 19 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, and made a game-winning layup in a 122–121 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-dennis-schroder-stuns-grizzlies-with-game-winning-steal-and-score-to-end-11-game-win-streak|title=Dennis Schroder stuns Grizzlies with game-winning steal and score to end 11-game win streak|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=20 January 2023|access-date=20 January 2023}}</ref>

Schröder was also a big factor in the [[Lakers]] struggling return to the playoffs after missing last year's [[2022 NBA playoffs|playoffs]]. During their play-in game on 11 April 2023 against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Dennis scored 21 points on 41.7% field goal shooting, along with 75% three-point shooting, including a tie-breaking corner three-point shot in regulation and the winning two free throws in overtime, clinching the 7th seed in the Western Conference and successfully securing a spot in the [[2023 NBA playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beacham |first=Greg |date=12 April 2023 |title=LAKERS OUTLAST WOLVES IN OT THRILLER FOR WEST NO. 7 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/min-vs-lal-0052200121 |access-date=23 November 2024 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:20230825 Basketball World Cup 01.jpg|thumb|250px|Schröder (right) with Germany alongside Japanese player [[Yuta Watanabe]] and Japanese prime minister [[Fumio Kishida]] in 2023]]
Schröder has been a member of the [[Germany national basketball team|German national under-18]] and [[Germany national basketball team|German national under-20]] teams. He played in the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] and helped the German team to fifth place, averaging 6.1 points, 2 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 14.6 minutes on the court. On 27 July 2014, he made his debut for the senior [[Germany national basketball team]] in a game against [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]].<ref>[http://mahr.sb-vision.de/dbb/html/herren/spieler/spielespieler.aspx?spnr=276 Spiele von Denis Schroeder (10)] {{in lang|de}}</ref>

Schröder played at [[EuroBasket 2015]], in the group stage that was hosted in [[Berlin]]. Germany did not qualify for the knock-out stage and finished on the 18th place in the final rankings.

He returned for [[EuroBasket 2017]], leading Germany to the quarterfinals and averaging a team-high 23.7 points and 5.6 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dennis SCHRODER (GER)'s profile|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Dennis-Schroder|website=FIBA EuroBasket 2017}}</ref>

Schröder had expressed a desire to play for Germany at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]]; however, the German Basketball Federation was unable to meet the financial insurance requirements.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barkas |first=Aris |date=16 July 2021 |title=Dennis Schroder will not compete in the Olympics |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/olympic-games/1229740/dennis-schroder-will-not-compete-in-the-olympics/ |access-date=23 November 2024 |website=eurohoops.net}}</ref>

He returned to [[EuroBasket 2022]] and led Germany as captain<ref>{{Cite web |title=Schröder führt Deutschland bei Basketball-EM an |url=https://www.spiegel.de/sport/basketball/basketball-dennis-schroeder-zum-kapitaen-der-nationalmannschaft-ernannt-a-5ad9514a-05b3-4d69-8ce5-5e119fadc94f |access-date=30 August 2025 |website=spiegel.de |date=17 August 2022 |language=de}}</ref> to third place,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Germany hold off Poland comeback to claim third place |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/germany-hold-off-poland-comeback-to-claim-third-place |access-date=19 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=18 September 2022}}</ref> being named to the [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team]] in the process.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Willy Hernangomez earns TISSOT MVP award to lead TISSOT All-Star Five in Berlin |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/willy-hernangomez-earns-tissot-mvp-award-to-lead-tissot-all-star-five-in-berlin |access-date=19 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=18 September 2022}}</ref> The run included a famous win over [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]] in the quarterfinals, which had [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] on the roster. Schröder averaged team highs of 22.1 points and 7.1 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Germany at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/team/Germany |access-date=19 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>

Schröder led the German national team to their first [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|World Cup]] title at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. The team went undefeated, defeating top-ranked teams such as [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australia]] and the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]]. After the final between Germany and [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]], he was named [[FIBA World Cup MVP]] and to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team]], averaging 17.9 points and 6.7 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dennis Schroder – Player Profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/189145/Dennis-Schroder |access-date=10 September 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>

At [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]], Schröder was the flag bearer for Germany along with [[judo]]ka [[Anna-Maria Wagner]].<ref name="Aussiedlerbote.com"/> After going unbeaten in Group B and beating Greece in the quarterfinals, Germany lost to France, 69–73, in the semifinals. In the bronze medal game, Germany lost to Serbia 83–93. For his play, Schröder was named to the [[FIBA Men's Olympics All-Star Five|FIBA Olympics All-Star Five team]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Fegers |first=Lukas |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympia 2024 - Guerschon Yabusele mit spektakulärem Poster-Dunk über LeBron James: "Werde ich zu Hause aufhängen" |url=https://www.eurosport.de/basketball/olympia-paris-2024/2024/guerschon-yabusele-mit-poster-dunk-uber-lebron-james-werde-ich-zu-hause-aufhangen_sto20028423/story.shtml |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=eurosport.de |language=German}}</ref>

Schröder had another successful tournament at [[EuroBasket 2025]], as he led Germany to their first European title since 1993. He scored 16 points and had 12 assists in the [[EuroBasket 2025 final|final]], which Germany won 88–83 over [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-14 |title=Germany win incredible Final against Türkiye |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/germany-win-incredible-final-against-tuerkiye-eb-25 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=www.fiba.basketball}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the tournament, he was named the [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP]] following his averages of 20.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, 7.2 assists and 0.8 steals. He became the third German player to win the award, after [[Chris Welp]] in 1993 and [[Dirk Nowitzki]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-14 |title=Dennis Schroder named TISSOT MVP of FIBA EuroBasket 2025 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/dennis-schroder-named-tissot-mvp-of-fiba-eurobasket-2025 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=www.fiba.basketball}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup Germany vs Serbia 20-27.jpg|thumb|Schröder and his family]]

Schröder is married and has three children.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goon |first=Mike |title=Dennis Schröder rejoins Lakers after birth of third child |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/12/04/dennis-schroder-returns-to-lakers-after-birth-of-third-child/ |website=The Orange County Register |access-date=14 September 2023 |date=4 December 2022}}</ref>

Schröder became known earlier in his career for his "signature" patch of bleached blonde hair which he adopted upon leaving Germany for the United States.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dawson |first=Brett |title=What to know about Dennis Schroder, luxury tax and the Thunder's busy trade week |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/article/5602177/what-to-know-about-dennis-schroder-luxury-tax-and-the-thunders-busy-trade-week |access-date=18 November 2021 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=21 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Craft |first=Dorian |title=Dennis Schröder convinced teammate to get blonde streak |url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2019/11/28/dennis-schroder-convinced-teammate-to-get-blonde-streak/ |access-date=18 November 2021 |work=OKC Thunder Wire |date=28 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |title=Who's been Celtics' most impactful player in 2021–22? The answer might surprise you |url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/whos-celtics-most-impactful-player-204548382.html |access-date=18 November 2021 |publisher=[[Yahoo!]] |date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119111145/https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/whos-celtics-most-impactful-player-204548382.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> It came at the suggestion of his mother who thought it would help people to recognize him in public.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bucher |first=Ric |title=Dennis Schroder Is Going to Be a Star, and He's Making Sure Everyone Knows It |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2690155-dennis-schroder-is-going-to-be-a-star-and-hes-making-sure-everyone-knows-it |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=10 October 2023 |date=3 February 2017}}</ref>

Schröder is a devout Muslim.<ref name=timur/><ref>{{cite news|last=Trister|first=Noah|title=Muslim athletes in US hope for continued acceptance|url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/5d88ae86269049899f5e3bfae2b0e557/muslim-athletes-us-hope-continued-acceptance|access-date=8 February 2016|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=15 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219062612/http://bigstory.ap.org/article/5d88ae86269049899f5e3bfae2b0e557/muslim-athletes-us-hope-continued-acceptance|archive-date=19 December 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He prays before games and before going to sleep.<ref name=timur/> Schröder is a [[teetotaler]] and has never consumed alcohol in his life.<ref name=timur/>

Schröder missed games on two different occasions due to [[COVID-19]] protocols in place. In May 2021, he said that he was the only Lakers player who had not been vaccinated against the virus.<ref>{{cite web |last=Faigen |first=Harrison |title=Dennis Schröder says he didn't have COVID, isn't vaccinated, but can't miss time again in confusing postgame remarks |work=Silver Screen and Roll|publisher=SB Nation |date=2021-05-15 |url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2021/5/15/22438022/dennis-schroder-covid-19-protocols-nba-playoffs-vaccine-comments-lakers |access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>

After the Nets were eliminated from the 2024 playoffs, Schröder joined FC Germania Bleckenstedt soccer team of the German [[Landesliga Braunschweig]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gharib |first=Anthony |date=2024-05-31 |title=Dennis Schroder makes professional soccer debut for German club in sixth division |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40252054 |access-date=23 November 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
